## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

13	`actions_list list_workflow_runs` with `per_page: 5`, got the overflow, and retried 23s
14	later with `per_page: 3` — **exactly 395,103 characters both times.** `per_page` does not
15	shrink these payloads; the per-object field set does. So:
16	
17	- Pass a **`fields` subset** on every `search_issues` / `list_issues` / `search_repositories`
18	  call — `["number","title","state"]` is enough for almost everything Claudinite tasks do.
19	  Dropping `body` alone is usually the whole difference; the same session's third
20	  `search_issues` call, identical but for `fields`, came back fine.
21	- `actions_list` has **no `fields` and no `minimal_output`** — `per_page` is its only knob and
22	  it doesn't work. Don't retry it smaller. Either narrow with `workflow_runs_filter`, or take
23	  the overflow as the answer and query the spilled file directly
24	  (`python3 -c "import json; …"` or `jq` over the `tool-results/*.txt` path in the error).
25	  That fallback is what finally worked, ~35s after the first attempt.

27	  `get`, whose body plus every field is what overflows.

30	
31	`curl … | tar -xz` of a repo tarball returns 403 through the network egress proxy. Use
32	`git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` instead, which works through the
33	proxy and yields the same tree.

36

When the primary source for a person's background is blocked, **do not substitute a

wrong, and the page had already shipped in a PR. Stripping them cost a second commit

paragraph — it is a public claim about a named person that they never made. The person
is in the conversation; one question is cheaper than any research. (The site-specific
form of this now sits in `product-wiki/product-requirements/` as a reviewed

# session-tooling — rules

## A GitHub MCP list read blows the token cap — `fields` is the size knob, not `per_page`

Any `mcp__github__*` read that returns a *list* of objects here returns the objects whole,
and the result is routinely 80KB–400KB — over the cap, so nothing reaches the session and
the body is spilled to a `tool-results/*.txt` file instead. Eight captured sessions between
2026-07-30 and 2026-08-12 hit it twelve times, across four different tools:
`search_repositories` (80KB, 86KB), `pull_request_read` `get` (158KB, 157KB, 168KB),
`search_issues` (112KB, 106KB) and `actions_list` `list_workflow_runs` (395KB, twice).

The trap is that the obvious knob is the wrong one. On 2026-08-12 a session called
`actions_list list_workflow_runs` with `per_page: 5`, got the overflow, and retried 23s
later with `per_page: 3` — **exactly 395,103 characters both times.** `per_page` does not
shrink these payloads; the per-object field set does. So:

- Pass a **`fields` subset** on every `search_issues` / `list_issues` / `search_repositories`
  call — `["number","title","state"]` is enough for almost everything Claudinite tasks do.
  Dropping `body` alone is usually the whole difference; the same session's third
  `search_issues` call, identical but for `fields`, came back fine.
- `actions_list` has **no `fields` and no `minimal_output`** — `per_page` is its only knob and
  it doesn't work. Don't retry it smaller. Either narrow with `workflow_runs_filter`, or take
  the overflow as the answer and query the spilled file directly
  (`python3 -c "import json; …"` or `jq` over the `tool-results/*.txt` path in the error).
  That fallback is what finally worked, ~35s after the first attempt.
- For a PR, prefer the narrow method (`get_files`, `get_commits`, `get_check_runs`) over
  `get`, whose body plus every field is what overflows.

## `codeload.github.com` is blocked here too

`curl … | tar -xz` of a repo tarball returns 403 through the network egress proxy. Use
`git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` instead, which works through the
proxy and yields the same tree.

## `enable_pr_auto_merge` never arms here — skip straight to a direct merge

When the task's own spec authorizes landing without human review (the growth tasks do),
don't retry `enable_pr_auto_merge` — poll `pull_request_read` `get_check_runs` until the
required check *completes* successfully, then `merge_pull_request` with `squash` directly.
Escalate `needs-human` only when the task requires a reviewer.

## The mounted `.claudinite/shared/` is code without docs — and its runners are silent when clean

Two ways the engine mount misleads a session that goes reading it, both paid for
on 2026-08-01:

1	// The scheduler's GitHub WRITES — the small set of issue mutations both dispatch
2	// mechanisms make, over the injected `gh` reader from signals/gh.mjs. Reads live
3	// with their callers; these are here so the slot machinery and the work-item queue
4	// share one implementation of each, rather than two that drift.
5	//
6	// LABEL WRITES ARE GRANULAR, ALWAYS (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §4, RESEARCH §2): add
7	// and remove NAMED labels (POST/DELETE), never write the label SET (PUT). A
8	// set-write replaces from a stale snapshot and clobbers concurrent transitions —
9	// a bug class GitHub's own CLI shipped (cli/cli#4861) — and with a scheduler run and
10	// several executors all moving labels at once, that is a correctness rule rather
11	// than a style preference.
12	
13	// Ensure every label exists before any is applied. Load-bearing, not cosmetic:
14	// GitHub does not create a label when you apply one (the issues API 422s on an
15	// unknown label), so the thing that assigns a label must guarantee it first.
16	// Idempotent (201 created / 422 already exists are both success) and self-healing
17	// — a deleted label reappears on the next run.
18	export async function ensureLabels(gh, repo, labels) {
19	  for (const { name, color, description } of labels) {
20	    const res = await gh(`/repos/${repo}/labels`, { method: 'POST', body: { name, color, description } });
21	    if (res.status === 201) continue;                       // created to spec — nothing further
22	    if (res.status === 422) {
23	      // The NAME is taken; that says nothing about the colour or description. A
24	      // label GitHub auto-created (applying an unknown name to an issue mints it
25	      // grey `ededed`, no description) would keep those defaults for good, because
26	      // POST 422s forever. So reconcile the shape, not just the existence — that
27	      // is what makes the self-healing claim above true for drift and not only for
28	      // deletion. PATCH is idempotent: an already-correct label is a no-op write.
29	      const fix = await gh(`/repos/${repo}/labels/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, {
30	        method: 'PATCH', body: { color, description },
31	      });
32	      if (fix.status !== 200) console.log(`! could not reconcile label "${name}": ${fix.status}`);
33	      continue;
34	    }
35	    console.log(`! could not ensure label "${name}": ${res.status}`);
36	  }
37	}

40	  gh(`/repos/${repo}/issues/${number}/labels`, { method: 'POST', body: { labels: [name] } });

1	// The machine-readable records a task's execution leaves in an Actions log
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2), and the parsers that read them back.
3	//
4	// TWO FAMILIES, ONE OF THEM HISTORICAL. `claudinite-task-run` was the SLOT
5	// scheduler's own line, one per due task per run; the slot scheduler is retired
6	// (#974) and nothing writes that line any more. The parser stays, and only the
7	// parser: Actions logs from before the retirement are still inside their retention
8	// window, and the usage fold still counts them. Nothing new should be taught this
9	// shape — `claudinite-task-exec` below is the live record.
10	//
11	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
12	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside.
13	
14	// The five things a slot scheduler run could do with a due task. One name per
15	// outcome, used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no
16	// mapping table between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
17	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
18	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an agent session ran this task.
19	  'agent',
20	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (code-work is the
21	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose code-work requested no agent phase.
22	  // Kebab, not the declaration field's `code_work`: this word is a WIRE token,
23	  // constrained to the line format's `[a-z-]+` charset.
24	  'code-work',
25	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
26	  'skipped',
27	  // Its code-work failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
28	  'failed',
29	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
30	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
31	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
32	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
33	  'deferred',
34	]);
35	
36	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
37	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
38	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
39	
40	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
41	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
42	// half-parsing it.
43	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
44	const VERSION = 'v1';
45	
46	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
47	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
48	// printed nothing at all.
49	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
50	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
51	);
52	
53	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
54	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
55	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
56	// The code phase has been renamed twice, and job logs outlive both renames:
57	// `preprocess` (pre-2026-08-06) and `prework` (pre-2026-08-18) are the earlier
58	// words for what is now `code-work`. Runs logged under either still parse, each
59	// normalized straight to the canonical word.
60	// Exported because the outcome words are also the usage aggregate's counter KEYS,
61	// and that file holds rows written under the older words. Its decode renames them
62	// by this same map, so a rename never silently drops a historical count.
63	export const LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze({ preprocess: 'code-work', prework: 'code-work' });
64	
65	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
66	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
67	  if (!m) return null;
68	  const [, pack, task, slotId, word] = m;
69	  const outcome = LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES[word] ?? word;
70	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
71	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
72	}
73	
74	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
75	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
76	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
77	  const out = [];
78	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
79	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
80	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
81	  }
82	  return out;
83	}
84	
85	// --- executor-side execution records ------------------------------------------
86	// The historical records above say what the retired slot scheduler DID with a due
87	// task; these record what an EXECUTOR SESSION did with the work it ran. Printed by executor-side code
88	// (resolve-dispatch on a terminal verdict, record-exec.mjs at convergence), they
89	// land in the session transcript, ride to the conversation-logs branch with the
90	// executor's capture step, and the usage fold counts them deterministically —
91	// the "task statuses out of the conversation logs" half of the census (owner,
92	// 2026-08-06). Same single-home rule: renderer and parser sit here together.
93	
94	export const TASK_EXEC_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
95	  // The dispatch ran to completion within its ceiling; the issue was closed.
96	  'success',
97	  // The run failed (task failure or ceiling violation); converged to needs-human.
98	  'failed',
99	  // The dispatch named a task the repo no longer carries (file gone, pack
100	  // undeclared) — the executor closed the issue as obsolete. Not a failure.
101	  'task-gone',
102	  // The dispatch was malformed (bad path shape, unparseable declaration) and was
103	  // converged to needs-human without running.
104	  'invalid',
105	]);
106	
107	export const TASK_EXEC_TAG = 'claudinite-task-exec';
108	
109	// The bracketed field is the OCCURRENCE'S IDENTITY, which is a different thing under
110	// each dispatch mechanism: a slot id (`d2026-08-06`) where slots decide what runs, and
111	// the work item's issue number (`#867`) where the queue does. `slotId` keeps its name
112	// for the fielded records that already carry one; what it must never become is a
113	// constant, since it is the only join from a record back to the work it describes.
114	export const renderTaskExec = ({ pack, task, slotId, status }) =>
115	  `${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} ${pack}/${task} [${slotId ?? 'unknown'}] ${status}`;
116	
117	const EXEC_LINE_RE = new RegExp(
118	  String.raw`(?:^|\s)${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
119	);
120	
121	export function parseTaskExec(line) {
122	  const m = EXEC_LINE_RE.exec(line);
123	  if (!m) return null;
124	  const [, pack, task, slotId, status] = m;
125	  if (!TASK_EXEC_STATUSES.includes(status)) return null;
126	  return { pack, task, slotId, status };
127	}
128	
129	export function parseTaskExecs(text) {
130	  const out = [];
131	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
132	    const rec = parseTaskExec(line);
133	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
134	  }
135	  return out;
136	}
